curl_note: The script requires Bash, cURL, OpenSSL and base64. Replace ASSET and ACCOUNT in the script, and ensure the signed query is encoded exactly as sent by cURL.
legacy_intro: This directory contains a signed HTTP script for diagnosing the legacy account-secret API. For application integration, use the Python, Go, Java or Node.js SDK.
legacy_config: Create an application in Application Management and authorize the target asset accounts. Set the endpoint, application AK/SK and organization ID below; replace every placeholder with its actual value before running.
targets: The examples query asset ubuntu_docker and account root by default. Replace them in the example with real authorized names. Run commands from the repository root. Example output contains secrets; do not send it to application logs.
legacy_response: The response id identifies the application, not an account revision. A null secret can reflect the server secret-view setting. These examples do not receive credential events, report applied revisions or execute application commands.
legacy_errors: For 401, check AK/SK, organization, host time and the signed URL. For 403, check application status and account authorization. For 400, check asset/account selectors and query encoding. Do not log secrets or Authorization headers. Account names and asset names must match the application’s authorized resources.
policy_access: The signature details and protocol table below are diagnostic references. Use SDK methods for credential policies, or use the Go pam-agent through JSON files, EnvironmentFile or Unix Socket.
signature: Sign requests with HMAC-SHA256 in the header order below. Include the encoded path and query in request-target, SHA-256 of the exact body in Digest, a unique UUID in X-JMS-Request-ID, an HTTP UTC Date, X-JMS-Client-Version, X-JMS-Protocol-Version: 1 and X-JMS-Config-Schema-Version: 0 for SDKs. API and WebSocket use the application AK/SK and a stable, unique instance_id; refresh the signature for each request or reconnect.
confirmation: Fetch the target account with `account_id`. Apply and verify the application change, then report `success` or `failed` using `event_id`. A delivery receipt or successful fetch does not mean the application succeeded. Events and reconnect snapshot items include `event_id`, `account_id` and `account_revision`. Verify the account version before applying it. Restart and manual switch commands must first be claimed with `running`. Make application handlers idempotent; a reconnect may repeat an event.
receipts: A received receipt only means an event was read. Send received with event_id on the same WebSocket before handling business events; snapshot and pong require no receipt. Reconcile the snapshot on every connection and reconnect, process credential.updated, and handle revocation or configuration changes.
python_intro: Python 3.9+ provides the credential-policy SDK. The Go pam-agent delivers credentials through local files, fixed actions or a local Socket without a Python runtime. Foreground runs support Linux, macOS and Windows; the built-in systemd installer is Linux-only.
agent_setup:
[Linux x86_64 (amd64)](/download/pam/pam-agent-linux-amd64) · [Linux ARM64](/download/pam/pam-agent-linux-arm64) · [SHA256SUMS](/download/pam/SHA256SUMS)

```bash
# Run in the directory containing the downloaded PAM Agent and SHA256SUMS.
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64) agent_arch=amd64 ;;
  aarch64|arm64) agent_arch=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "Unsupported CPU architecture"; exit 1 ;;
esac
sha256sum --ignore-missing --check SHA256SUMS && \
sudo install -m 0755 "./pam-agent-linux-${agent_arch}" /usr/local/bin/pam-agent
```
agent_confirm: Fetch the target account with `account_id`. Apply and verify the application change, then report `success` or `failed` using `event_id`. A delivery receipt or successful fetch does not mean the application succeeded. Events and reconnect snapshot items include `event_id`, `account_id` and `account_revision`. Verify the account version before applying it. Restart and manual switch commands must first be claimed with `running`. Make application handlers idempotent; a reconnect may repeat an event.
recovery: The PAM Agent reconciles at startup, on relevant notifications and at the configured interval (300 seconds by default). Temporary outages retain still-authorized credentials. Explicit revocation or application disable blocks local reads and removes managed store files, even if the next refresh fails. Business configuration files remain under the application administrator’s control. Notification traffic does not postpone periodic service updates. SIGINT/SIGTERM closes the server and event reader.
sdk_setup: Requires Python 3.9+. Use the application Python or virtual environment. Install the client source shipped by the same Core using the commands below; released v1.0.2 packages do not include managed callbacks. Replace jumpserver.example.com with your Core address. Keep the extracted jms-pam-clients directory with your application, including the Go module replacement path.
sdk_config: `jms_pam_config.py` is an application configuration file, not part of the `jms-pam` PyPI package. Download it from the application access wizard and save it next to your application script, or create it with the content below and replace every placeholder with the actual application identity. Do not commit or log `client_options`. Use a stable, unique `instance_id` per replica.
sdk_run: For an interactive test, start Python from the directory containing `jms_pam_config.py`, then run the example below. For a script, save the example as `app.py` alongside the configuration and run `python3 app.py` instead. If `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jms_pam_config'` occurs, check the file name and location; reinstalling `jms-pam` will not create this file.
event_processing: Implement the account-change callback below, then start the managed listener. The SDK handles snapshots, fresh account lookup, account/version validation, retry, command claims and event results. Return only after validating the real connection, switching the application pool and releasing old connections. Python and Node.js use subclass hooks, Go uses OnAccountChanged, and Java uses AccountEventListener. The placeholder fails until business switching is implemented.
apply_error: Implement and verify application credential switching
account_listing: Use the account listing methods to discover the application’s current authorized pull scope. Listings return account and asset metadata plus related push policies, without retrieving passwords or recording credential fetches. Accounts without policies are included. The full-list method follows all pages; the page method returns `count` and `accounts` (Go returns the slice and total separately). Defaults are limit 200 and offset 0; limit is 1–500 and search is at most 128 characters, matching account name, username, asset name or address. Duplicate accounts, incomplete results and changing totals raise an error; retry the whole listing if authorization changes. Use an account ID with the account-fetch method when its secret is needed. Examples require SDK source containing these new methods; published version 1.0.2 does not yet provide them in Python, Java or Node.js.
application_info: Read the authenticated application ID, name, organization and authorized account/policy counts with get_application; get_client_info returns only the current replica’s registration, type and versions. Policy listing returns the entire visible bound list, including disabled policies; search matches policy names or keys. Fetch a policy using exactly one of its ID or base policy key, rather than an account push key. Rotation policies require authorization for both accounts and the active account. Subscription counts include only accounts currently authorized to this application. These calls return metadata without secrets and do not fetch credentials or confirm application changes. As with account queries, the replica is registered on first access. They require updated Core and SDK source; the published 1.0.2 does not yet contain these methods.
sdk_errors: The client closes HTTP sessions and event streams with with or close. clone creates an independent session. HTTP, network, authentication and decoding failures raise PAMError with code, status_code, detail and original_error. Retry transient errors at the application boundary; handle authorization denial explicitly and keep credentials out of logs.
compatibility: New code uses snake_case keyword methods and dataclass attributes. The original credential.v1 request-object API remains available with DeprecationWarning. SDK version 1 uses the same protocol as the PAM Agent; sync_agent accepts KnownRevision values for retained and delivered revisions.
sdk_receipts: The SDK automatically sends a best-effort received receipt before yielding a business event. No additional receipt is required from the application. A receipt means only that the event was read, not that credentials were applied; it does not replace confirmation. Reconcile the initial and reconnect snapshots; snapshot and pong require no receipt.

Python and Node.js use subclass hooks, Go uses OnAccountChanged, and Java uses AccountEventListener. The placeholder fails until business switching is implemented.

A delivery receipt or successful fetch does not mean the application succeeded. Events and reconnect snapshot items include `event_id`, `account_id` and `account_revision`. Verify the account version before applying it. Restart and manual switch commands must first be claimed with `running`. Make application handlers idempotent; a reconnect may repeat an event.
native_errors: HTTP, network, authentication and response decoding failures use the SDK exception/error type with code and HTTP status. Close streams and clients when finished. Clones have independent lifecycles. Retry transient failures at the application boundary and never log secrets or authentication headers.
native_compatibility: All SDKs use protocol version 1; PAM Agent configuration uses schema version 1. A client_upgrade_required response (HTTP 426) requires checking compatibility and upgrading. Unknown optional fields and notification events are tolerated; unsupported policy modes must not be applied or confirmed. Received event receipts are sent automatically and do not prove credential application. Client metadata may include server_capabilities. Missing or null means unknown; unknown names are tolerated. Capabilities describe server features, not authorization.
native_agent:
Run the standalone PAM Agent on the application host; Python is not required. Follow the sections below to install it, select delivery, configure business actions and verify the result.

Use `account_id` for application credential queries and local rule selectors. For file delivery, configure a fixed business path in the rule, such as `/etc/sample-app/database.json` or `/etc/sample-app/database.env`. An A/B rule declares one account ID with `allow_account_switch: true`; it keeps the output path fixed while the delivered content records the currently active `account_id`.
native_install: Install the client source shipped by the same Core using the commands below; released v1.0.2 packages do not include managed callbacks. Replace jumpserver.example.com with your Core address. Keep the extracted jms-pam-clients directory with your application, including the Go module replacement path.
managed_title: Listen for updates and switch connections
managed_intro: Implement the account-change callback below, then start the managed listener. The SDK handles snapshots, fresh account lookup, account/version validation, retry, command claims and event results. Return only after validating the real connection, switching the application pool and releasing old connections. Python and Node.js use subclass hooks, Go uses OnAccountChanged, and Java uses AccountEventListener. The placeholder fails until business switching is implemented.
managed_behavior: The account callback runs serially behind a bounded event queue. Failed account updates retry with 1–30 second backoff. Success is reported only after the business callback returns; a failed result upload retries the upload without repeating a completed action in the same listener. Commands execute only after an accepted claim; failed command actions are not automatically repeated. Applied accounts are reported as a complete usage snapshot; A/B switches replace the current account. Implement revoked-account cleanup for scope removals. Usage reporting, fetches and file delivery never themselves confirm application success. Low-level streams and legacy credential hooks retain explicit confirmation. Business handlers must remain idempotent across restarts.
event_liveness: Event connections send application ping messages at 10-second intervals while idle and reconnect after approximately 30 seconds without messages. Reconnect uses 1–30 second exponential backoff and fresh signatures. Reconnect snapshots restore current state; past events are not replayed.
managed_lifecycle_python: watch_events waits until stopped. start_events returns before initial synchronization is complete; wait for application readiness before serving requests. One managed listener is allowed per client. stop_events and close wait for an active hook; a hook may stop its own client. clone rebuilds subclass state; override it for additional constructor dependencies.
managed_lifecycle_go: WatchEvents waits in the calling goroutine. StartEvents returns before initial synchronization is complete. One managed listener is allowed per client. Stop and Client.Close request cancellation; call Wait externally to join handlers. Do not call Wait from a handler, and make long operations honor the context.
managed_lifecycle_java: watchEvents waits in the calling thread. startEvents returns before initial synchronization is complete. One managed listener is allowed per client. EventSubscription.close and Client.close stop and wait for active handlers; a handler may close its own subscription or client. awaitTermination must be called externally.
managed_lifecycle_node: watchEvents awaits completion without blocking the event loop; startEvents returns before initial synchronization is complete. One managed listener is allowed per client. Async hooks are awaited serially and receive an AbortSignal. close requests cancellation synchronously; externally await subscription.stop() or done to join. A hook may await stopEvents, but must not await its own done. clone returns a new base Client.
latest_credentials_behavior: SDK credential getters request the API first. A successful fetch replaces the retained value without allowing revisions to move backwards. Only a timeout, network error or HTTP 5xx permits fallback to a previously fetched value for the same selector, marked as local; retained values have no time expiry. SDK caches are client-local memory: clones and restarts start empty. HTTP 401/403/404 or credential_not_found (HTTP 400) clear retained credentials and raise. HTTP 426 and malformed successful responses raise without using fallback; a missing optional metadata endpoint does not clear credentials. PAM Agent persists accounts declared by store/services in protected state; an undeclared on-demand query is not automatically retained. Explicit revocations take effect before HTTP refresh, including while offline. Push snapshots do not define the full authorization scope of stored accounts; successful reconciliation checks the current application authorization.
live_refresh: With managed event listening enabled, snapshot and credential.updated automatically fetch the current credential, replace the retained value and then invoke the business hook. A failed refresh leaves the previous value in place and retries. The PAM Agent also refetches on update notifications and retains its previous credentials during backend outages. Refresh and manual switching use the live-only calls below; a retained password must not be treated as a newly fetched revision or automatically confirmed.
agent_config_format: `update_config.format` defaults to `auto`; omitting it has the same effect. Detection uses the file extension: `.txt`, `.env` and `.properties` use `env` (`KEY=value`); `.yml` and `.yaml` use `yaml` (top-level `KEY: value`, written as quoted strings). For other extensions, explicitly choose `env` or `yaml`. Mapped fields must already exist exactly once; unrelated settings are preserved. INI sections and nested YAML require `files` + `template_file` to generate the whole file, or a custom `script`. Environment-file updates take effect after the application rereads the file or restarts.
event_results: Fetch the target account with `account_id`. Apply and verify the application change, then report `success` or `failed` using `event_id`. A delivery receipt or successful fetch does not mean the application succeeded. Events and reconnect snapshot items include `event_id`, `account_id` and `account_revision`. Verify the account version before applying it. Restart and manual switch commands must first be claimed with `running`. Make application handlers idempotent; a reconnect may repeat an event.
event_compatibility: `get_credential` and key-based confirmation remain available for older integrations. New integrations use `get_account` and `confirm_event`. The event-result workflow requires the corresponding Core update; SDK 1.0.2 alone cannot add this server capability.
status_reporting: Report a complete snapshot of the application state and the account IDs currently in use. States: `starting`, `running`, `degraded`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `error`. An empty account list clears previous usage. Call on state changes or from your own heartbeat; no background reporting is started. Python, Java and Node.js return false on network/API failures, including an older Core without this endpoint; Go provides `TryReportStatus` for the same behavior. Strict variants expose failure details. Invalid arguments are rejected. Requests use the configured HTTP timeout; keep reporting off latency-sensitive paths. Reporting never fetches secrets, confirms rotation or invalidates retained credentials. Use machine-readable `error_code` only, without secrets or exception messages. `get_client_info` / `GetClientInfo` / `getClientInfo` return the last reported snapshot and its timestamp.
agent_rules_title: Update business configuration and A/B rotation
onboarding:
1. Create an application and authorize the accounts it may retrieve.
2. Enable Account credential change notifications in the application when immediate updates are needed. This covers all authorized accounts. A/B switching uses a separate rotation policy.
3. Download the application access materials and protect its AK/SK. Give each replica a stable, unique instance ID.
agent_overview: Run the standalone PAM Agent on the application host; Python is not required. Follow the sections below to install it, select delivery, configure business actions and verify the result.
agent_bootstrap: Run in the directory containing the downloaded `pam-agent.json`. The Linux service commands below require root and systemd. For foreground mode, use the executable for your operating system and architecture.
agent_queries: Run CLI and Socket requests as the configured application user. `get_accounts` lists authorized account metadata; `get_secret` retrieves a secret on demand, including pull-only accounts. It writes the secret to stdout, so use it only in a private terminal. Replace the Socket path in foreground mode.
agent_validation:
1. Verify the instance is online and its authorized account scope is correct.
2. Enable application notifications, change an authorized account credential and check its version in the delivered file or Socket. Inspect per-instance receipts and results in the application event history.
3. For A/B switching, verify that the running application uses the new account and releases old connections before confirming success. Receipt, fetch and delivery do not prove business success.
sdk_workflow: Use only the retrieval section for pull-only access. For pushed updates or A/B rotation, implement the managed business callbacks and start listening. The SDK handles protocol and event results; the application validates and switches real connections. These examples reflect the current source: install a matching Core and SDK build before using new APIs; released 1.0.2 packages do not include all of them.
sdk_validation:
1. Replace the account placeholder with an authorized account ID and verify a real connection without logging the password.
2. If listening for updates, verify initial synchronization and an authorized-account update or A/B switch; complete the business callback before expecting a successful event result.
3. Check the instance usage/status and event result separately. A fetch or usage report does not confirm credential application.
agent_confirmation: Validate the running connection and switch the application before confirming an event. Use either a successful `app_check` with `confirm_on_success: true`, or explicit confirmation after business verification. Do not call the confirmation API from a synchronous check script. Local results are persisted: `confirmed` means Core accepted the result; `pending` is retried.
source_install: If this Core does not provide the source download endpoint, or for offline deployment, obtain its matching client source at `/path/to/pam-clients` and run the following from the application directory. Replace the path with your actual checkout.
credential_check_step: Optional: validate the new login before changing files.
update_config_step: Update the existing business file using field mappings, a template or a script.
reload_service_step: Reload/restart the configured service or run a fixed script.
app_check_step: Verify the running business connection; only then confirm application success.
foreground_binary: Save the foreground binary as `pam-agent` (`pam-agent.exe` on Windows); on Linux/macOS give it execute permission with `chmod 0755 ./pam-agent`.
agent_environment_file: EnvironmentFile writes the username, password and account metadata as plaintext `KEY=value` entries in a private `.env` file (0600). The business systemd service must explicitly reference this file with `EnvironmentFile=`. systemd loads it into that service process environment when starting the process; it does not set global host variables. Restart the service after an update to refresh its main process environment. Reload alone does not replace an already running process environment.
store_model: `store` and `services` are independent. `store.accounts` is a string array: `["all"]` stores every authorized account, or list specific account IDs. Application notifications cover all authorized accounts when enabled. Local declarations control storage and business actions. On-demand access and scheduled synchronization also work with notifications disabled. Omit `store` for services-only use; an empty array stores nothing. Never combine `all` with IDs.
store_layout: Each stored account has its own file named by its actual account ID, including separate A/B accounts. Files contain plaintext credentials with mode 0600. A/B standby accounts being changed are temporarily unavailable. Successful authorization reconciliation removes revoked files. An unchanged reconciliation reads metadata without fetching passwords again; actual fetches remain audited and participate in rotation access observation.
services_model: Add the service objects below to `services`. Each service needs a unique stable `name`. `allow_account_switch` belongs to the service and defaults to false: when true, accounts with a unique A/B association follow the active account; other accounts remain fixed. Declaring A is sufficient. `update_on_notification` also belongs to the service and defaults to true. False defers business actions until scheduled reconciliation (300 seconds by default), while storage and authorization revocations still update. Each service tracks its own applied versions. Only successful application checks with `confirm_on_success: true` can automatically confirm a rotation, after every relevant service succeeds.
aliases_model: In `services.accounts`, use `id` to select an account. One account may use `username` / `secret` directly. Multiple accounts require unique aliases and qualified references such as `database.username` and `cache.secret`. Alias references stay stable across A/B switches. Optional selector `username` is a display hint only; actual values come from Core. Resolve every required account before writing the file, then run the service action once. Missing or ambiguous mappings fail before mutation.
services_upgrade: Core and PAM Agent use protocol version 1 and `version: 1`. Configure `store` and `services` independently; do not mix them with the older `delivery` / `rules` structure. Core supplies account scope and version metadata, never local executable paths. Restart the PAM Agent after editing its private configuration.
services_portable: For macOS, Windows or non-root Linux, initialize once with `init-local`, then reuse the generated private configuration with `run --local`. Standard JSON and environment files are supported; systemd actions require the Linux service.
store_all_label: All accounts authorized for this application, independently of the notification setting.
store_selected_label: Only the explicitly declared account IDs.
agent_onboarding:
1. Create an application and authorize the accounts it may retrieve. Account IDs below are JumpServer account IDs.
2. Declare accounts in store/services. Enable Account credential change notifications in the application for immediate updates to all authorized accounts; bind an A/B rotation policy only when switching is required.
3. Download the identity configuration from the application access wizard and protect the AK/SK. `instance_id` is optional.
pull_interval: `pull_interval` is the global polling interval in seconds, a positive integer with a default of 300. The PAM Agent synchronizes immediately at startup, then checks account and credential versions at this interval, fetching secrets only when versions or the active account change. Services with `update_on_notification: false` update on the next poll; notifications do not postpone it.
services_field_names: New configurations use `update_config` → `reload_service` → `app_check`: update the business file, reload/restart the service (or run a fixed script), then verify the running application. These names require an updated PAM Agent. `services` accepts only these three step names; old names are rejected.
configuration_blocks_help: The complete Linux/systemd example below includes application identity, polling, standard credential files, the local API and a business service. Replace the identity, account ID, operating-system user, paths, service name and check script with your actual settings; deploy the check script first. Set `services` to `[]` if you only need files or the local API. The following sections explain each block; all blocks belong to the same configuration file.
store_purpose: `store` delivers credentials as standard JSON or environment files for applications that read credentials from files. It controls which accounts are written, the output directory, format and file owner. Updating an existing business configuration or reloading a service belongs in `services`.
socket_purpose: `socket` configures the local Unix Socket interface for health checks, account listing, on-demand credential retrieval, account usage reporting and application-result confirmation. Applications can query the socket without enabling `store`. Retrieval follows the application authorization in Core; `store.accounts` selects file output and does not restrict the API account scope.
socket_model:
`path` defaults to `/run/jms-pam-agent/agent.sock`. `owner` controls socket access and the default owner of business output files; if omitted, it uses `store.owner`, then the PAM Agent process user. Omitting `socket` uses these defaults; it does not disable the interface. `init-local` sets the socket to `<directory>/run/agent.sock` and the owner to the current user.

When running without root, omit both `store.owner` and `socket.owner` to use the current user. `init-local` sets both to the current user automatically. When running as root, specify the application user if it needs to read the files or access the socket. The owner setting does not switch the PAM Agent process user.
agent_instance_id: `instance_id` is optional. When omitted or empty, PAM Agent generates `<hostname>-<4 random hexadecimal characters>`, for example `orders-pod-a1b2`. An explicit `instance_id` or `--instance-id` takes precedence. Installation and `init-local` save the generated ID in their output configuration. Direct runs retain it in the private state file and reuse it after restart without rewriting the input configuration. K8s replicas can share configuration with this field omitted; each replica needs its own writable state directory. A new replica with no retained state generates a new ID.
update_config_methods: Each object in `services` describes one business service. Choose exactly one `update_config` method: `file + fields_map` edits existing fields, `files + template_file` renders complete files, or `script` runs a custom update. Replace that service’s `update_config` with one of the fragments below.
update_config_template: Use templates to generate complete nested JSON, INI or other configuration files. Set `files[].format` to `template` and `template_file` to an absolute local path. Rendering precedes atomic file replacement with mode 0600; omitted `owner` defaults to `socket.owner`. The `json` function quotes and escapes JSON values.
update_config_payload_keys: Template `.Credentials` and script `credentials` are keyed by the declared `services.accounts[].id`, not alias. Replace `<primary-account-id>` with the real ID. During A/B switching, the key stays the declared A ID while `AccountID` (`account_id` in scripts) identifies the active account.
update_config_script: Declare one output with `target`, or several with `targets`, so PAM Agent can back them up before mutation. Deploy `script.path` as a local executable. `args` holds fixed parameters; credentials arrive as JSON on stdin. `timeout_seconds` accepts 1–300 seconds, default 120. The script runs as the PAM Agent user. Exit 0 means success; nonzero exit or timeout fails and retries, so updates must be idempotent.
update_config_script_example: This Linux/macOS Python 3 example updates database fields in an existing JSON file, preserves other settings and ownership, and atomically replaces it with mode 0600. Prepare the target directory and initial JSON file, deploy the executable script, and grant execute permission. Custom scripts manage their own output format, permissions and ownership.
update_config_apply: Template or script success only completes the configuration update. Configure `reload_service` and `app_check` in the same service when reload or business verification is needed. Validate the configuration before restarting PAM Agent:
overview_relationships:
1. **Account authorization** controls which accounts the application may fetch on demand. Authorize the application before installing a client.
2. **Account credential change notifications** is an application-level switch covering all authorized accounts. Use it when applications should react to password changes; no subscription policy is required.
3. **A/B rotation** is a separately bound policy for switching between two accounts before changing the original password. Both accounts must be authorized. Open the policy’s operation guide for its cycle, waiting conditions, cancellation and recovery.
overview_choices:
| Method | Use when | Start here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SDK | You can change the application code and let it connect to JumpServer. | Select SDK integration and your programming language. Implement a managed account-change callback for automatic updates. |
| PAM Agent | You need local credential files, business configuration updates or a local Socket, and want to keep JumpServer keys outside business code. | Select Agent integration, install the Agent and configure store, socket and services as needed. |
| Socket API | Business-managed connections through the local Agent; no JumpServer SDK or AK/SK in the business. | Socket API access; declare a service with delivery: socket. |
overview_flow:
1. Create an application, authorize accounts and download its private identity configuration.
2. Choose SDK or PAM Agent, install the matching client, fetch an account and verify a real connection.
3. For automatic updates, enable application notifications and implement the business change. For A/B switching, also bind a rotation policy and enable following its current account.
4. Verify one account update or A/B switch: the application uses the new credential, old connections are released and the business result is successful. Reception, fetching and file delivery alone are insufficient.
overview_reading: Agent integration covers deployment, files, local APIs and business actions. SDK integration covers installation, managed callbacks and language-specific APIs. Events and commands is the shared reference for event payloads, snapshots, receipts and administrator commands. The operation guide inside each rotation policy explains its own cycle, blockers and recovery.
protocol_intro: This reference applies to all SDK languages and PAM Agent. Prefer managed SDK callbacks or configured Agent services for normal integration; use the raw protocol only when implementing an event consumer yourself.
protocol_events:
| Event | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| credential.updated and snapshot items | Fetch the named account, verify its version, apply it and report the business result. Managed SDK callbacks handle the protocol. |
| app.scope.updated | Reconcile scope and remove invalid state. Removing a rotation binding does not revoke account authorization. |
| `rotation.*` (such as `rotation.started` and `rotation.completed`), `credential.change.*` (such as `credential.change.started` and `credential.change.completed`) | Update progress, logs or alerts. Do not repeat credential application or confirm business success for these notifications. |
| credential.switch.requested and app.restart.requested | Administrator commands for selected instances: claim, execute and report the command result. |
protocol_fields:
| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| event_id | Event identity for receipts and application results. snapshot itself has no receipt; credential items can have their own event_id. |
| event / occurred_at | Event type and publication time. |
| account_id / account_revision | Concrete target account and password version. A fresh account revision must match before application. |
| credential_key / revision | Policy publication metadata for A/B rotation. Ordinary account notifications use account revisions. Do not mix the two version domains. |
| credential_mode | alternating_rotation for an A/B policy; subscription for application-level account notifications, without a subscription policy. Application-wide events may use null. |
| account_switch.account_ids | Accounts associated with an A/B switch. |
| operation_id | Correlates events belonging to one change operation or rotation cycle. |
| command_id / expires_at | Administrator command identity and execution deadline. Commands have a separate result API. |
protocol_commands:
Administrators send commands from the application’s Send event action and choose instances and an expiry time.

- credential.switch.requested asks the instance to apply the rotation policy’s **already published** account and version. It does not start a rotation or select another account.
- app.restart.requested asks the application to run its supported restart action and verify health. The SDK application must implement that handler; Agent support depends on its local service configuration.

Managed SDK handlers claim and report commands automatically. Raw consumers use the signed client API:

1. GET /api/v1/accounts/credential-client/commands/ with instance_id to poll pending commands; connected instances can also receive them over WebSocket.
2. POST /api/v1/accounts/credential-client/command-result/ with instance_id, command_id and status: running. Execute only if accepted is true.
3. After actual application switching or a successful restart health check, report status: success through the same command-result API; on failure report failed with a safe error_code. A received receipt or confirm_event alone does not replace command-result reporting.

Expired commands cannot be claimed. Duplicate delivery must not repeat a claimed action. Failed command actions are not automatically repeated; inspect the application before sending a new restart request.
protocol_scope_legacy: Current names are app.scope.updated, app.restart.requested, rotation.verify.started/failed/cancelled and rotation.waiting_for_app. Old application prefixes, rotation.verification names and configuration.updated normalize to the new names without changing event IDs. credential.revoked is no longer emitted and remains only for older Core integrations and historical records.
protocol_snapshot: Core sends snapshot on connection, reconnection and scope changes. Its credentials include all authorized accounts when application notifications are enabled, plus active authorized A/B rotation policies bound to the application. Process each item like credential.updated using event_id, account_id and account_revision. The snapshot also includes authorized_account_ids; get_accounts lists authorized account metadata. Removing a rotation policy binding does not revoke account authorization.
protocol_catalog_intro: Every Core application event, administrator command and connection control message is listed below, with compatibility entries separated. This is the complete reference; rotation details explain how the events relate to that policy workflow.
protocol_catalog_accounts_help: credential.updated applies credentials. app.scope.updated and snapshot reconcile scope: detach a missing rotation policy while preserving use of authorized accounts. Only actual account authorization removal disables local access, clears retained credentials and asks the application to release connections.
protocol_event_credential_updated: Current credentials or published account changed; fetch and apply the named account.
protocol_event_credential_revoked: Retired: current Core no longer sends this event. Use app.scope.updated and snapshot; retained only for older Core integrations and historical records.
protocol_event_app_scope_updated: Account authorization, notification settings or rotation bindings changed. Use authorized_account_ids to determine account access, then snapshot to reconcile notifications and rotation following. Removing a binding must not close an otherwise authorized account connection.
protocol_catalog_changes_help: General task lifecycle notifications for progress and alerts. Do not fetch again or report application success for these notifications; apply credentials on credential.updated or snapshot.
protocol_event_credential_change_started: A password-change task is queued or running; the remote password may not have changed yet.
protocol_event_credential_change_complet: The password-change task succeeded; this is not proof that applications applied the credentials.
protocol_event_credential_change_failed: The password change failed or could not be verified; inspect the task and remote account.
protocol_catalog_rotation_help: These notifications explain cycle progress and outcomes. Application switching follows credential.updated or snapshot, not a second action on each progress event.
protocol_event_rotation_verify_failed: Backup verification failed; no switch is published.
protocol_event_rotation_started: The rotation cycle has published the target account and started switching.
protocol_event_rotation_waiting_for_app: Waiting for required application instances to apply and confirm the target.
protocol_event_rotation_source_waiting: Observing successful secret fetches for the original account after publication.
protocol_event_rotation_source_ready: The original account no-fetch window and required client conditions allow password change.
protocol_event_rotation_completed: The original account password change was verified and the rotation completed.
protocol_event_rotation_failed: Rotation entered a password-change failure or recovery-required state.
protocol_event_rotation_force_stopped: An administrator ended the cycle without waiting for remaining recovery confirmations.
protocol_catalog_commands_help: Claim with running, execute only when accepted is true, then report the command result. These are independent of automatic rotation progress.
protocol_event_credential_switch_request: Apply the already published account and version on selected instances; this does not start a rotation.
protocol_event_app_restart_requested: Execute the supported application restart action and verify health.
protocol_catalog_connection_help: SDK and Agent manage liveness and receipts. snapshot and pong need no received receipt; snapshot credential items are applied separately.
protocol_event_snapshot: Core sends the current notification scope and authorized account IDs on connection, reconnection or scope changes.
protocol_event_ping: The client sends an application-level keepalive to Core.
protocol_event_pong: Core replies to an application-level ping.
protocol_event_received: The client acknowledges reading an event; it does not report business success.
protocol_catalog_legacy_help: Legacy event names and old preparation-cycle entries, not a workflow for new integrations. Current Core no longer emits credential.revoked; new rotation cycles verify the backup before publishing the switch.
protocol_event_rotation_preparation_star: Legacy preparation began aligning applications to the current account.
protocol_event_rotation_accounts_aligned: Applications finished alignment in the legacy preparation flow.
protocol_event_rotation_standby_waiting: Legacy preparation is observing secret fetches for the standby account.
protocol_event_rotation_preparation_read: Legacy preparation is ready; no switch or password change is implied.
protocol_event_rotation_verify_skipped: Backup-account login verification skipped by credential policy.
socket_intro: Use a local PAM Agent from any application without installing a JumpServer SDK or storing application AK/SK in the business process. The Agent handles Core authentication, authorization, credential refresh, A/B resolution and result retries. The application owns real connections and business validation.
socket_transport: The transport is a Unix Domain Socket (AF_UNIX), not TCP. Connect to its filesystem path; no IP address or port is opened. HTTP/JSON requests and the WebSocket event channel share this socket. The localhost URL supplies the HTTP Host only. Agent-to-Core traffic still uses HTTPS/WSS.
socket_config: Add a socket service to the Agent configuration. Use the same account declarations and allow_account_switch rules as file delivery. The declared A ID remains the map key while account_id identifies the active A/B account. Socket services cannot also configure update_config, reload_service, credential_check or app_check. restart_supported is an explicit opt-in for business restart commands.
socket_workflow: Connect, read the initial snapshot, retrieve the delivery credentials, verify new real connections, replace business connections and release old sessions, then submit success. Receiving a notification or fetching a password never proves that the business has switched. A failed callback submits failed and is retried after the Agent backoff.
socket_snapshots: Every connection starts with the latest snapshot; this is current-state reconciliation, not historical replay. delivery contains metadata only, including delivery_id, declared-account keys and exact account/policy revisions. Revocations are delivered even during a Core outage; revoked_account_ids requires closing old sessions. With no complete credentials, a delivery may be absent while refresh is pending. Each independently applied business instance needs its own service_id. Only one WebSocket connection per service is accepted.
socket_results: Return the exact delivery_id with success or failed. The Agent persists accepted results before reporting to Core and waits for every relevant service before confirming a credential event. accepted means locally saved, not that Core has already accepted it. Duplicate successful results are idempotent; a superseded version returns HTTP 409. After failed, retry_ready becomes true after 1–30 seconds. If a result response is lost, retry the result rather than repeating successful business work. Callbacks must be idempotent: a crash between a business effect and its local ACK cannot guarantee exactly-once execution. Snapshot fields received, credentials_read and result track distinct local stages. core_status separately tracks pending, confirmed, failed or not_required. Send the received operation to record a receipt; credential retrieval also records receipt. Neither operation confirms business success.
socket_commands: Commands are claimed by the Agent before delegation. Restart commands appear in commands only for services with restart_supported=true. Report command.result after restart and readiness validation; success or failure is persisted and Core reporting is retried without executing the command again. A/B switch commands reuse credential delivery and its business result. Expired commands cannot be acknowledged.
socket_status: Business status is separate from credential confirmation. Use starting, running, degraded, stopping, stopped or error and a short non-secret error_code. Account usage is updated only after business success, and the Agent aggregates all service reports. GET /v1/usage returns the aggregate. The existing POST /v1/usage replaces the instance-wide explicit account declaration; it does not acknowledge events.
socket_boundary: Unix socket ownership is the access boundary. service_id identifies a business consumer, not a separate security identity: processes able to open the same socket share the application authorization. Keep unrelated trust domains on separate Agent instances/sockets. Events omit passwords; retrieve credentials explicitly and never log them. Polling the service snapshot and posting results is supported when a language has no Unix-socket WebSocket client.
socket_example: The Python example uses websockets, not a JumpServer SDK. By default it only observes metadata and never acknowledges business success. Implement the Business callbacks and call run(socket_path, service_id, business) for real processing. On a new business process, initialize connections from the current delivery even when it was applied by the previous process. Persist business-side delivery IDs when crash-safe de-duplication is required.
